questions.question:
Identify the tense and voice used in the sentence:

"Early prototypes, such as horse-drawn wagon ways in 16th-century Europe, represented rudimentary precursors to modern trains..."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2** i.e '**Simple Past Active**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the sentence, the verb **"represented"** is used in the simple past tense.
 
• The subject **"Early prototypes"** is actively performing the action of representing.
 
• There is no auxiliary verb (like "have" or "was/were") indicating a perfect or continuous tense, nor is there a passive construction ("was represented").
 
• **Active voice** means the subject does the action, which is the case here.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Past Perfect Passive:** Would use "had been represented," which is not present in the sentence.
 
• **Present Perfect Active:** Would use "have/has represented," which is also not present here.
 
• **Past Continuous Passive:** Would use "was/were being represented," which does not match the structure of the sentence.

__
 
• The phrase **"utilizing wooden rails to minimize friction"** modifies the verb **"represented"** by explaining how the action was performed.
 
• Such phrases function adverbially, providing information about the manner or means of the action.
 
• It does not modify a noun (so it is not an adjective clause), nor does it function as a subject or an object in the sentence.
 
• It answers the question **how** the prototypes functioned as precursors to modern trains.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Option 2.**

• **Adjective clause:** Would begin with a relative pronoun like "which" or "that" and modify a noun. This phrase does not do that.
 
• **Noun clause:** Typically acts as a subject or object and starts with words like "that" or "what." This is not the case here.
 
• **Gerund phrase acting as the subject:** Would appear at the beginning as the main subject, e.g., "Utilizing wooden rails was important." In this sentence, the phrase explains how something was done, not what did it.

options.text: The rubbish was being thrown away

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "We threw away the rubbish."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the rubbish" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "threw away" to "was thrown away" (past simple passive).
 
• The subject "we" is omitted because it is not essential for the meaning in passive voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"The rubbish was thrown away."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"The rubbish thrown away." – This is incorrect as it lacks the auxiliary verb "was" needed for passive voice.
 
• **Option 3: **"The rubbish was being thrown away." – This is incorrect as it implies a continuous action, which is not stated in the original sentence.
 
• **Option 4: **"The rubbish will be thrown away." – This is incorrect as it changes the tense to future, which is not consistent with the original sentence in past tense.

Choose the correct indirect speech of the sentence:

She said, "Why didn't anyone inform me about the change?"

options.text: She asked why had no one informed her about the change.

She asked why didn't anyone inform her about the change.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** Indirect speech is used to report what someone has said without quoting their exact words.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Change in tense:** In indirect speech, past perfect tense is used to replace the past tense when the reporting verb is in the past. Here, "didn't inform" becomes "had informed."
 
• **Change in pronouns:** The first-person pronoun "me" changes to "her" to match the subject of the reporting clause (She).
 
• **Question to statement:** The sentence is converted into a statement form. "Why didn't anyone inform me" becomes "why no one had informed her."
 
 
 
• **Correct Sentence:** She asked why no one had informed her about the change.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** She asked why had no one informed her about the change.
 
 
• Incorrect word order. In indirect speech, the auxiliary verb "had" should follow "no one," not precede it.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** She said why was no one informing her.
 
 
• Incorrect tense. "Was informing" is present continuous, which does not match the reported past event.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** She asked why didn’t anyone inform her about the change.
 
 
• Incorrect tense and structure. The question is not properly converted to a statement form, and "didn't" should not be used in indirect speech.
